papers.title: Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
papers.abstract: Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker parameters. Notably, our result also holds for distributions whose marginals are "locally independent" and "approximately identically" distributed. It is not known whether such distributions fool general DNFs, which makes the derandomization via DNF-fooling techniques unavailable. Our proof of this derandomization is via the method of moments, which might be of independent interest. We apply this result to obtain improved separations between non-monotone arithmetic circuits and the radical of monotone circuits. Specifically, we construct an explicit family of multilinear polynomials $P_n$ that have small non-monotone arithmetic circuits such that any power of $P_n$ cannot be computed by monotone arithmetic circuits of sub-exponential size. This improves on a recent result of Cavalar, Fabris, Mukhopadhyay, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff (STOC 2026), who proved a non-explicit separation that was quasipolynomial. Our construction uses Nisan-Wigderson designs with an additional linear-algebraic expansion property.

papers.title: Complexity Framework For Forbidden Subgraphs V: Beyond Simple Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate how allowing self-loops and multi-edges (i.e. moving from simple graphs to pseudographs) impacts the complexity of graph problems on finitely defined monotone graph classes. We do this by extending the C123-framework beyond simple graphs. We use several testbed problems to illustrate some of the new and varied behaviours introduced by the transition to pseudographs. We show that Pseudograph Matching Cut and Pseudograph d-Cut are C123-problems. Consequently, for every finite set HH of simple graphs, we obtain a complete complexity classification for these problems on HH-subgraph-free graphs. This sharply contrasts with their simple-graph counterparts, which are not C123-problems and their complexity remains open even for classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph H. We also show that Pseudograph Stable Cut is not a C123-problem. Nevertheless, for graph classes defined by a single forbidden subgraph, the problem mirrors the C123 classification; this correspondence already fails for sets of size 2. This gives the first example of a problem that aligns with C123-problems for a single forbidden subgraph but not for larger sets. Motivated by the interpretation of Stable Cut as a surjective homomorphism to a partially reflexive path, we also study surjective homomorphisms to partially reflexive cycles on k vertices with one irreflexive vertex. These problems share structural similarities with Pseudograph Stable Cut. We prove that for k at least 6, they are NP-complete on triangle-free pseudographs. However, unlike Pseudograph Stable Cut, they are polynomial-time solvable on all graph classes with bounded-degree.

papers.title: Single-Vertex Metropolis on Minor-Free Graphs: A General EPTAS
papers.abstract: We consider a class of combinatorial optimization problems where the goal is to find a largest induced subgraph with a prescribed property. We assume that the property is preserved by taking induced subgraphs and disjoint unions, holds for all edgeless graphs, and can be tested in polynomial time. We study the single-vertex Metropolis process for this class of problems. We show that on graphs excluding an arbitrary fixed minor $H$, this process is a randomized efficient polynomial-time approximation scheme. Starting from any feasible solution on a graph with $n$ vertices, it finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-approximation within $\exp(O_H(\varepsilon^{-2})) n(n+\log(1/\delta))$ steps with probability at least $1-\delta$. This includes maximum independent set, maximum induced forest, maximum induced bipartite subgraph, and maximum induced subgraph of degree at most one. The proof uses improving exchanges on one fixed division of the input graph into regions. A recursive separator construction performs each exchange inside a region of size $r$ in at most $2r$ moves, with temporary loss $O_H(\sqrt r)$. We count move sequences through each transition and bound the probability of avoiding all near-optimal states. The general theorem bounds the number of Metropolis steps in terms of the temporary loss along improvement paths. We extend the result to bounded weight imbalance and give a weighted-star obstruction for unrestricted weights.

papers.title: Supersaturation and reconfiguration diameter of independent transversals
papers.abstract: Consider the collection of independent transversals of a vertex-partitioned graph of maximum degree $\Delta$. It is a classic result that when all parts have size at least $2\Delta$, the collection is nonempty. Recently, it was found that if the parts have size at least $2\Delta+1$, then every pair of independent transversals is connected, within the collection, by a sequence of one-vertex reconfigurations. We prove, among other results, that there are exponentially many independent transversals when the parts have size at least $2\Delta$, and that the reconfiguration diameter is at most linear in the number of parts when the parts have size at least $4\Delta$.

papers.title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
papers.abstract: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line. The 19 displayed algebraic certificates comprise 18 improvements and one closed-form reproduction; they include HJ(4,3)>=164, HJ(5,4)>=7418, and HJ(5,6)>=34034. The underlying period-p construction also proves kappa_ow(t,r)>=p-1 for the one-weight bracket ceiling, in particular kappa_ow(5,4)>=7416 and kappa_ow(5,6)>=34032. Warm breakout-weighted tabu search on the type simplex gives HJ(3,4)>=51. Whole-colouring local search gives W(8,3)>522, W(11,3)>1193, and W(17,3)>3620. All accepted certificates are available separately and are checked by direct enumeration; unresolved searches are reported as UNKNOWN, not UNSAT.

papers.title: On (Pathwidth, Clique)-boundedness
papers.abstract: We prove that every $(\pw,\omega)$-bounded class of graphs has bounded tree-independence number, answering a question of Be\v{s}ter \v{S}torgel, Dallard, Lozin, Milani\v{c}, and Zamaraev. We deduce this from a bound on the tree-independence number of graphs with neither $\B_\rho$ nor $K_{\sigma,\sigma}$ as an induced minor, where $\B_\rho$ is the complete binary tree of height $\rho$ and the bound depends only on $\rho$ and $\sigma$. We then obtain an asymptotically sharp bound on the path-independence number of $n$-vertex graphs in any $(\pw,\omega)$-bounded class. The lower-bound examples also give counterexamples to a conjecture of Hickingbotham and Joret. We further prove that, for every forest $F$ and every $\ell\in\N$, there is a constant $k=k(F,\ell)\in\N$ such that every graph $G$ with no induced theta or $\ell$-long prism and no induced subgraph isomorphic to $F$ satisfies tree-independence number at most $k$. This proves a strengthened form of a conjecture of Chudnovsky, Hajebi, and Trotignon. Finally, for every integer $s\ge2$, we characterize the forests $F$ for which excluding $F$ as an induced minor and $K_{s,s}$ as an induced subgraph bounds tree-independence number. This extends the characterization of Bonnet, Duhamel, and Hickingbotham, who considered bounded pathwidth with $K_{s,s}$ excluded as a subgraph.

papers.title: Sharp lower bounds for weighted bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
papers.abstract: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts the sizes of which differ by at most one. We prove that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most an odd positive integer $k$, with arbitrary nonnegative real edge weights, has a bisection of weight at least $(k+1)/(2k)$ times its total edge weight. The corresponding bound $(k+2)/(2(k+1))$ for even $k$ follows immediately. Both coefficients are best possible. Somewhat surprisingly, these are exactly the sharp coefficients known for maximum weighted cuts, despite the additional balance requirement.

papers.title: Heap-type permutation generation with a prescribed final arrangement
papers.abstract: Heap's algorithm generates all permutations of an array of n items, obtaining each one from its predecessor by a single swap. We determine the net permutation applied to the array by every complete recursive call: a transposition when the number of items is odd and at least three, and a cycle through all items when it is even. We show that the output of each call is a concatenation of right cosets of the symmetric group on one item fewer, and we prove a general formula: the order in which the items are parked at the last position may be chosen freely, every such order corresponds to exactly one valid schedule, and it determines the net permutation of the call. Two variants follow. In the cyclic variant a complete sweep over an even number of items rotates the array by one position. In the extremal variant, for even n, a sweep started from the identity ends in the lexicographically largest arrangement that any single-swap enumeration can leave; by a parity argument this is the reversal exactly when n is congruent to 2 modulo 4. The construction of the extremal variant is proved correct when n is divisible by 4 and verified by computer for all even n up to 10000.

papers.title: Rado's covering problem for cubes and balls: a survey
papers.abstract: What is the largest constant $c\in [0,1]$ with the property that every finite collection $\mathcal{C}$ of axis-parallel squares in the plane admits a disjoint sub-collection $\mathcal{S}$ occupying at least a fraction $c$ of the area covered by $\mathcal{C}$? This problem was first raised by T.~Rad\'o in 1928, who was motivated by a classical covering lemma in real analysis due to Vitali. R.~Rado later generalized the problem from axis-parallel squares in the plane to homothetic copies of any given convex body $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where now we are looking for an optimal constant $F(K)$. In this paper we survey the literature on this problem, with a focus on the case where $K$ is a cube or a ball in the high-dimensional regime $d\rightarrow \infty$. The estimates that we currently have for cubes are much more precise than those for balls: namely if $Q^d$ is a $d$-dimensional cube, then \[ (e^{-1}+o(1))\frac{2^{-d}}{d \log{d}} \leq F(Q^d)\leq 2^{-d}, \] while denoting $B^d$ a $d$-dimensional Euclidean ball, then \[ 2.910^{-d} \leq F(B^d) \leq 2.447^{-d}.\] Except for the upper bound for cubes, which is classical, the other estimates are due to the authors.

papers.title: Optimal self-orthogonal binary linear codes
papers.abstract: We complete the determination of the minimum possible length of eight-dimensional binary self-orthogonal codes with given minimum distance. For dimension nine we give exact values and bounds for minimum distance at most $64$. By exploiting the geometric reformulation of linear codes as multisets of points, we fully redo the classification for dimension at most seven in a simplified and computer-free manner. As a by-product we prove the non-existence of $[93,9,44]_2$ codes and show several divisibility results for putative optimal nine-dimensional binary codes.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: An upper bound on non-overlapping codes
papers.abstract: Non-overlapping codes (also known as bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a binary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{5}{6e} +O(n^{-1})\right)\frac{2^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$. This improves, by a factor of $5/6$, the best previously known bound due to Levenshtein (1970). The paper builds on work by Fimmel, Michel, Pirot, Sereni and Str\"ungmann (2019), and by Stanovnik, Mo\v skon and Mraz (2024).

papers.title: Non-isomorphic graphs have distinct vertex-Ramsey classes
papers.abstract: For a graph $H$, its $k$-colour vertex Ramsey class is the set of all graphs $G$ such that any colouring of the vertices of $G$ in $k$ colours results in a monochromatic (induced) copy of $H$. We prove that for any $k$, the $k$-colour vertex Ramsey classes of any non-isomorphic graphs are distinct. Moreover, we show that this property does not hold when individual graphs are replaced with families of graphs.

papers.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
papers.abstract: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold. Then the Nakayama-type argument established by Gu et al., together with the classical Whitney presentation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian, gives a proof of such a presentation.

papers.title: Optimal Network Design under Node Failures
papers.abstract: Networks are frequently constructed before it is determined which nodes will persist. We address the design problem in scenarios where nodes fail independently, links are costly and must be established in advance, and the benefits to surviving nodes diminish with distance. Examples include supplier, interbank, and infrastructure networks. Among all possible networks, the complete, star, and empty configurations are each welfare-optimal within specific ranges of link costs. However, with four or more nodes, failures introduce a range of costs in which every optimal network contains more links than the star but fewer than the complete network. At the lower end of this range, we show that the optimal networks are exactly those obtained by removing a matching from the complete network. We develop an exact algorithm for complete multipartite networks. It finds an optimal network by dynamic programming in a number of operations that grows with the fourth power of the number of nodes, although the class itself grows superpolynomially. For networks with up to six nodes, restricting the design to this class results in no loss under explicit conditions. We also characterize pairwise-stable networks within this class and establish their existence for every level of link cost. Finally, we quantify the cost of misjudging failure risk. Overestimating node survival leads to overbuilding and can yield lower welfare than building nothing, whereas underestimating it never does. Under uncertain failure risk, design should therefore favor conservative reliability estimates.

papers.title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
papers.abstract: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $\Delta(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

papers.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly. In this paper we close this gap and determine the system of length sets when the class group is isomorphic to $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$.

papers.title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
papers.abstract: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls. We also give a characterization of $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of any dimension with neighborly boundary.

papers.title: Cohomological VC-density: Bounds and Applications
papers.abstract: The concept of Vapnik-Chervonenkis (VC) density is pivotal across various mathematical fields, including discrete geometry, probability theory and model theory. In this paper, we introduce a topological generalization of VC-density. Let $Y$ be a topological space and $\mathcal{X}$ a family of closed subspaces of $Y$. For each $p \geq 0$, we define a number, $\mathrm{vcd}^{p}_{\mathcal{X}}$, which we refer to as the degree $p$ VC-density of the family $\mathcal{X}$. The classical notion of VC-density within this topological framework can be recovered by setting $p=0$. Our definition of degree $p$ VC-density extends to higher orders as well. For $p \geq 0$, $q \geq 1$, we define the degree $p$, order $q$ VC density $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$ of $\mathcal{X}$, which recovers Shelah's notion of higher order VC-density for $q$-dependent families when $p=0$. Our definition introduces a completely new notion when $p > 0$. We examine the properties of $\mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p$ (as well as $\mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}}$) when the families $\mathcal{X}$ are definable in structures with some underlying topology (for instance, the Euclidean topology for o-minimal structures over $\mathbb{R}$, the analytic topology over $\mathbb{C}$, or the \'{e}tale site for schemes over arbitrary algebraically closed fields). Our main result establishes that in any model of these theories \[ \mathrm{vcd}_{\mathcal{X}}^p \leq (p+1) \dim X, \] and more generally for any $q \geq 1$ \[ \mathrm{vcd}^{p,q}_{\mathcal{X}} \leq (p+q) \dim X. \] We give examples to show that our bounds are optimal. We also present combinatorial applications of our higher-degree VC-density bounds, deriving higher degree topological analogs of well-known results such as the existence of $\varepsilon$-nets and the fractional Helly theorem.

papers.title: Plane partitions and spin adapted quantum states
papers.abstract: We describe an explicit basis for the $\operatorname{SU}(2)$-invariant space of the exterior power $\wedge_{2k} \mathbb{C}^{2m}$ via the combinatorics of plane partitions. In quantum chemistry, this is the space of spin adapted quantum states of an electronic system with $m$ spin orbitals and $k$ electron pairs. We construct our basis by identifying the invariant space with an Artinian commutative ring called the excitation ring. We compute a Gr\"obner basis and enumerate its standard monomials via an explicit bijection to Dyck paths counted by the Narayana numbers.

papers.title: Macdonald intersections and the $N!/k$ conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Frobenius characteristic formula for the intersection of Garsia--Haiman modules predicted in the Science Fiction of Bergeron and Garsia. As a consequence, we resolve the $N!/k$ conjecture. The proof uses the geometry of the Hilbert scheme of points in the plane developed by Haiman.

papers.title: Counting formulas and refined generating functions for inversion-sequence Classes 152 and 207
papers.abstract: For the two Class 152 pattern sets, we prove that the common number of inversion sequences of length \(n\geq 1\) is \(a_n=1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\binom{2j}{j}\). The Class 152 proof uses first-descent and last-zero decompositions, with weighted Dyck paths evaluating the resulting generating functions. For Class 207, we prove equality of the three total-count series and give their common generating function as an explicit Lambert-series expression after the substitution \(z=q/(1+q)^2\). Complete legal-site and catalytic recurrences lead to a Lambert series for one class and \(q\)-product orbit sums for another. A cubic limit of the balanced nonterminating \({}_3\phi_2\) \(q\)-Saalschutz summation identifies these expressions. Fixed-maximum expansions, finite verification data, refined analytic obstructions, and signed specializations are recorded in the supplementary material.

papers.title: Co-edge-regular graphs with two $\lambda$-values and four distinct eigenvalues
papers.abstract: A connected $k$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is co-edge-regular if any two distinct non-adjacent vertices have the same number of common neighbors. For adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, let $\lambda(u,v)=|N(u)\cap N(v)|$. Ge and Koolen asked whether the theorem of Neumaier on strongly regular graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue extends to co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues in which $\lambda(u,v)$ takes exactly two values over the edges $uv$. In this paper, we answer this question. For every integer $t\ge2$ there is $n_t$ such that if $G$ is such a graph with smallest eigenvalue at least $-t$, $n\ge n_t$, and $k<n-2-(t-1)^2/4$, then either $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, or $G$ is obtained from a strongly regular graph with a Hoffman coloring by adding all edges inside the color classes. Consequently, $G$ is a clique extension of a strongly regular graph, a $p\times q$ grid with $p\ne q$, or the block graph of a resolvable Steiner $2$-design in which every parallel class is made into a clique.

papers.title: Resistance-regular graphs need not be regular
papers.abstract: A connected graph is resistance-regular if the sum of the effective resistances from a vertex to all other vertices does not depend on the vertex, or equivalently if the Moore-Penrose inverse of its Laplacian has constant diagonal. Walk-regular graphs have this property, and Zhou, Wang and Bu asked in 2016 whether every resistance-regular graph is regular, a question that also arises in the study of graphs with constant resistance curvature. We answer this question in the negative and examine both what resistance-regularity forces and how far from regular such graphs can be. On the spectral side, we prove that a connected graph is walk-regular if and only if the first $m-1$ powers of its Laplacian pseudoinverse have constant diagonal, where $m$ is the number of distinct nonzero Laplacian eigenvalues. Because resistance-regularity constrains only the first power, it forces regularity when $m\le2$ and allows at most two vertex degrees when $m=3$. Any non-regular resistance-regular graph has minimum degree at least $3$ and a connected complement, and an exhaustive computer search shows that it must have at least $13$ vertices. For every even $p\ge4$, we construct a resistance-regular graph on $4p$ vertices with degrees $2p-2$ and $2p-1$, obtaining closed formulas for its Laplacian spectrum and for all pairwise effective resistances. Using module blow-ups, we then construct $n$-vertex resistance-regular graphs whose two degrees differ by $(\sqrt{4n+1}-5)/4$ for infinitely many $n$, as well as examples with three and four distinct degrees, whereas the maximum and minimum degrees of any resistance-regular graph on $n$ vertices differ by less than $n/2$. We close by conjecturing that in a resistance-regular graph the sum of squared resistances at a vertex increases strictly with its degree.

papers.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
papers.abstract: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. In a smallest counterexample we find a $4$-connected planar part containing four vertices of degree five. Their neighborhoods meet the boundary in at most one vertex. This allows us to apply the planar configurations of Blanch\'e, Bonamy, and Bonichon and to realize the reduced graph as a minor of the original graph.

papers.title: The Conic Tverberg plus minus
papers.abstract: We prove a Tverberg type theorems: Given a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and an affine subspaces $L_1,...,L_m\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. In some conditions there is a partition $A_1, ..., A_m, B_1, ..., B_m$ of $A$ such that the sets $L_i\cup A_i\cup B_i$ for $i=1,...,m$ have common barycentre with negative masses in $B_i$ and positive masses in $A_i$. The case $B_1=...=B_m=L_1=...=L_m=\varnothing$ is Tverberg's classical theorem. The case $L_1=...=L_m=\varnothing$ gives a partial answer to the question of Barany-Soberon about the possible number of negative masses.

papers.title: Forbidden Substructures Preserved by the Blob Graph Operation
papers.abstract: The blob graph $G^\circ$ of a graph $G$ has a vertex for each non-empty connected vertex subset of $G$, with two distinct subsets adjacent whenever they intersect or are joined by an edge of $G$. This construction has been used in reductions from induced subgraph optimisation problems to maximum-weight independent set, where the preservation of forbidden substructures is essential. We completely characterise the graphs $H$ for which excluding $H$ from $G$ guarantees that $G^\circ$ also excludes $H$, under six containment relations. For subgraphs, minors, and topological minors, preservation holds exactly when $H$ has at most two vertices. For induced subgraphs, it holds exactly when $H$ is a linear forest. For induced topological minors, it holds exactly when $H$ is triangle-free and has maximum degree at most two. For induced minors, it holds exactly when $H$ is triangle-free and every neighbour of a vertex of degree at least three has degree exactly two. These classifications unify and extend preservation results previously established for particular forbidden graphs in algorithmic applications.

papers.title: Shifted Hankel determinants via Hankel continued fractions
papers.abstract: The Hankel determinants $H_n(F)$ of a power series $F(x)$, as well as the shifted ones $H_n^{(1)}(F)$ and $H_n^{(2)}(F)$, can be read off from its Jacobi continued fraction, provided that all $H_n(F)$ are nonzero. Without any condition on $F$, the Hankel continued fraction ($H$-fraction) still yields all $H_n(F)$. We show that the $H$-fraction of $F$ also determines the shifted Hankel determinants $H_n^{(1)}(F)$, $H_n^{(2)}(F)$ and the backward shifted ones $H_n^{(-1)}(F)$, and we give explicit formulas for them. As applications, we provide simple proofs of Hankel determinant evaluations that were previously established by means of complicated explicit $H$-fractions.

papers.title: Laplacian Eigenvectors of Generically Weighted Graphs Have Pairwise Distinct Coordinates
papers.abstract: Poignard, Pereira and Pade conjectured that, for a generic choice of the nonzero weights of a given graph, the Fiedler vector of the weighted Laplacian has pairwise distinct coordinates. We give a proof that also covers every nonconstant eigenvector. For each connected graph on n vertices we construct a nonzero homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients in the edge weights, of degree n(n-1)(n^2-n+2)/4, which vanishes at a positive weighting exactly when the Laplacian has a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvector with a zero coordinate, or a nonconstant eigenvector with two equal coordinates. The exceptional weights therefore lie in an algebraic hypersurface, which gives structural genericity in the sense of Poignard, Pereira and Pade; algebraically independent weights are never exceptional, and there are good integer weights not exceeding the degree plus one. The polynomial is a product of Krylov determinants. Its nonvanishing follows by induction on trees: when a leaf is attached with a small weight, a cut identity gives the first-order profile of the new eigenvector and separates the coordinates that coincide in the limit. Exact small cases show that exceptional weightings need not be symmetric.

papers.title: Perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and independence complexes of generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n,2)$
papers.abstract: We show that the perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and the independence complexes of the generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n, 2)$ are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres, and we determine the number and dimensions of the spheres. For the former we compute the initial values of Adamaszek's recursion for the independence complexes of cubes of cycles.
